tricks.description: You snip the wire fixed to a creature you have a String attached to within range, and its own body betrays it. Choose one effect below; the target resists with the listed saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}, and on a success it is unaffected. You must already have a String attached to the target to use this trick.
tricks.narration: A snip of the fingers on a wire you already laid, and whatever was holding them up simply is not. The sword leaves the hand, or the knees leave the argument.

options.name: Disarm (Wisdom save)
options.effect: On a failed save, the target drops one item of your choice that it is holding.

options.name: Trip (Constitution save)
options.effect: On a failed save, the target is knocked prone.

tricks.sheetSummary: Requires a String on the target. Choose one: Disarm (Wis save or drop one held item of your choice) or Trip (Con save or knocked prone). Success: no effect.

tricks.name: Dead Man's Hand
tricks.flavor: Aces and eights, face up on the table. Everyone at the game knows what that hand means, and so, now, do you.
tricks.description: You lay down a hand that should not exist — aces and eights, face up, in a fight nobody was playing cards in — and let its meaning land like a verdict. Choose one creature you can see within range. It makes a Constitution saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. On a failure it takes [[6d8]] psychic damage as the certainty of its own death arrives ahead of schedule, and it is stunned until the end of your next turn. On a success it takes half as much damage and is not stunned. Either way it is hurt: this is the biggest thing you do all fight, and it does not hinge on one roll.
tricks.narration: You deal it out onto whatever surface is nearest — a table, a crate, the floor between you — and you do not have to explain it. Everyone at a table knows that hand. So, somehow, does the thing you dealt it to.
tricks.sheetSummary: One creature. Constitution save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. Fail: [[6d8]] psychic and stunned until the end of your next turn. Success: half damage, no stun.

tricks.name: Doubled Image
tricks.flavor: Which one of you is real? Wrong question - ask which one of you the crowd is watching.
tricks.description: Illusory afterimages of yourself flicker into being every time you move, blurring exactly where your real body is. Attack rolls against you have disadvantage for the duration, unless the attacker doesn't rely on sight to locate you (a blind attacker, or one with truesight or another sense that sees through the illusion) or can otherwise track you by a non-visual sense.
tricks.narration: Afterimages of you flicker off every movement, half a beat behind and slightly to the left. Which one is real is the wrong question; the right one is which one anybody is actually swinging at.
tricks.sheetSummary: Attack rolls against you have disadvantage (no effect on attackers who don't rely on sight, e.g. truesight or blind).

tricks.name: Flash Powder
tricks.flavor: A pinch between two fingers, a snap of the wrist, and the world goes white and orange for exactly as long as you need it to.
tricks.description: You throw a pinch of flash powder that bursts into a searing white flash in a 10-foot radius centered on a point you choose within range. Each creature in that area makes a Dexterity saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. On a failure, a creature is blinded until the end of its next turn. On a success, it is unaffected. The burst is light and noise, not fire — it deals no damage; it just takes the crowd's eyes away for a beat.
tricks.narration: A pinch between two fingers, a snap of the wrist, and the world goes white and orange for exactly as long as it takes you to be somewhere else.
tricks.sheetSummary: 10-ft radius burst. Dex save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. Fail: blinded until end of its next turn. Success: no effect. Deals no damage.

tricks.name: Grand Guignol
tricks.flavor: Every wire you've laid snaps taut at once, and for one terrible instant every puppet on your stage dances the same violent step.
tricks.description: You sever every String at once, and the recoil slams each stringed body against itself. Every creature you currently have a String attached to within range is wrenched by its own wire: each makes a Strength saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. On a failure, a creature takes [[3d8]] physical damage, is knocked prone, and is restrained until it or another creature uses an action to cut it free. On a success, it takes half as much damage and is neither knocked prone nor restrained. You must have at least two Strings attached to cast Grand Guignol, and when it resolves the String on every creature it targets detaches and is consumed at once — leaving you to re-establish your control from scratch.
tricks.narration: Every wire you have laid snaps taut at once. For one terrible instant every puppet on your stage moves exactly as you meant it to and then does not move again, and the wires come away empty.
tricks.sheetSummary: Requires 2+ Strings attached; detaches and consumes the String on every creature it hits. Every Stringed creature in range: Str save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. Fail: [[3d8]] physical, prone + restrained (escape = an action to cut it free). Success: half damage only.

tricks.name: Idle Image
tricks.flavor: A little something to hold the audience's attention while your other hand does the real work.
components: Prop (a scrap of silk or a coin)
tricks.description: You conjure a harmless sound or image of an object no larger than a 5-foot cube within range - a burst of applause, a shimmering curtain, a shadow that looks like a second performer standing in the wings. The illusion has no substance and cannot deal damage, move on its own, or convincingly imitate a specific creature's voice or appearance beyond a rough silhouette. Any creature that uses its action to inspect the image can determine it is an illusion with a successful Intelligence (Investigation) check against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. The image lasts until you dismiss it (no action required), you move more than 30 feet from it, or its duration ends.
tricks.narration: A little something for the audience to hold on to while the other hand does the real work: a burst of applause from an empty corner, a curtain that is not there, a shadow crossing a doorway nobody is standing in.
tricks.sheetSummary: Harmless illusory sound or image (max 5-ft cube), up to 1 minute or until dismissed/out of range. No damage, no self-movement, no true creature mimicry. Investigation check vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}} to see through on close inspection.

tricks.name: Killing It
tricks.flavor: Every performer knows the feeling: the room is yours, the timing is perfect, and you could say anything right now and it would land. Tonight, it lands hard.
tricks.description: You spend banked Mirth on a bit that takes the whole room at once. Each creature of your choice within a 15-foot radius of a point you can see within range that can hear and understand you makes a Wisdom saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. On a failure it takes [[2d8]] psychic damage; on a success it takes half as much. Casting this costs 3 Mirth, spent whether or not anybody fails, and you may freely exclude your own company from the area — nobody has ever been hurt by a joke they were in on.
tricks.narration: You have the whole room and you know it. Whatever you say next goes through every one of them at the same moment, and the ones who are not in on it come away genuinely hurt.
tricks.sheetSummary: 15-ft radius. Creatures of your choice that can hear and understand you; allies can be excluded. Wisdom save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. Fail: [[2d8]] psychic. Success: half damage.

tricks.name: Lull
tricks.flavor: Watch the hand. Listen to the count. There is nothing in this room that needs you right now.
tricks.duration: Until the end of the target's next turn
tricks.description: You take one creature that can see and hear you within range through the old parlour routine — the voice, the count, the slow hand — and its shoulders come down. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. On a failure it is charmed by you until the end of its next turn: its speed becomes 0 and it cannot take actions or reactions, though it is fully aware and remembers everything afterwards. **Any damage ends the effect immediately**, so it removes a creature from the fight only for as long as your allies leave it alone — waking it is always an option and often the right one.
tricks.narration: The voice does the work. Their weapon lowers, their weight settles, and for a few seconds they stand in the middle of a fight looking mildly interested in nothing at all.
tricks.sheetSummary: Target must see and hear you. Wisdom save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}} or charmed until the end of its next turn: speed 0, no actions or reactions, still aware. ANY damage ends it immediately.

tricks.name: Marionette Hand
tricks.flavor: A hand that isn't there, hung on wires you never quite show the audience, doing the small work while you keep smiling.
tricks.description: You conjure a near-invisible puppet hand, hung on wires, in an unoccupied space you can see within range. It lasts for the duration, until you dismiss it (no action required), or until it ends up more than 30 feet from you. As a bonus action on your turn you can direct the hand: it flies up to 30 feet and manipulates one object — open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item, pour a flask, pull a lever, or carry an object weighing up to 10 pounds. The hand cannot attack, cannot activate magic items, and cannot wield a weapon or move a creature or anything a creature is holding.
tricks.narration: A hand that is not there, hung on wires you never quite show the audience, doing the small work at a distance — lifting a latch, sliding a bolt, carrying a cup — while both of yours stay visibly, innocently empty.
tricks.sheetSummary: Conjure a spectral puppet hand (up to 1 min, dismiss free). Bonus action to move it up to 30 ft and manipulate an object: open/carry (max 10 lb), stow/retrieve, pour, pull a lever. No attacks, no magic items, cannot affect creatures or held items.

tricks.name: Master of Ceremonies
tricks.flavor: You throw your arms wide, and for the length of the introduction, you are exactly who the room needs you to be.
tricks.description: You wrap yourself in a small illusion of bearing and reputation — a borrowed title, a fresh face, an unearned air of importance. For the duration, you have advantage on Charisma (Deception) and Charisma (Performance) checks, and your voice and appearance seem subtly different (the color of your eyes, the cut of your clothes, small mannerisms) to anyone who hasn't already seen through the act. This trick cannot make you pass for a specific individual.
tricks.narration: You throw your arms wide and borrow a reputation you never earned. For the length of the introduction you are precisely who the room needs you to be, and nobody thinks to check.
tricks.sheetSummary: Advantage on Deception and Performance checks; minor cosmetic disguise (not impersonation of a specific person).

tricks.name: Meat Shield
tricks.flavor: Why stop a blade when you can stand someone else in front of it? A yank of the wire, and the nearest enemy becomes a very reluctant barricade.
tricks.duration: Until the start of your next turn
tricks.description: You haul on the String fixed to a creature you have a String attached to within range, dragging its body where you want it and pinning it there as a living barricade. The target makes a Strength saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. On a failure, you drag it up to 15 feet — through spaces it could normally move through, without provoking opportunity attacks — to an unoccupied space of your choice, where it is restrained until the start of your next turn. While it is pinned this way its body is a shield: any creature has half cover against an attack or effect whose path passes through the meat shield's space. On a success, the wire snaps — the String detaches and nothing else happens. You must already have a String attached to the target to use this trick.
tricks.narration: Why stop a blade when you can stand someone else in front of it? You haul on the wire and drag the nearest unwilling volunteer into the space you did not want to occupy, and there they stay.
tricks.sheetSummary: Requires a String on the target. Str save. Fail: drag it up to 15 ft (no opportunity attacks) to a space you choose; it is restrained until the start of your next turn and its body grants half cover to anyone behind it. Success: the String detaches, no effect.

tricks.name: Night Terrors
tricks.flavor: The trick is not the thing you show them. The trick is that it keeps coming back once you have stopped showing them anything.
tricks.description: You leave something behind in a creature's head and let it work on its own. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}; on a success nothing happens and the trick ends. On a failure the horror settles in: at the start of each of its turns it takes [[1d8]] psychic damage, and at the end of each of its turns it may repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success. Because the target rolls against you again and again, this is the trick that keeps a Nightmare's other features fed.
tricks.narration: You put it there and then you walk away and talk to somebody else. It comes back to them at the worst moment of every round, and each time it costs them something.
tricks.sheetSummary: Wisdom save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}} or: [[1d8]] psychic at the start of each of its turns, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns to end it.

tricks.name: Now You Don't
tricks.flavor: The curtain drops for exactly one second. When it rises, you're not where the audience is looking anymore.
tricks.description: You vanish behind a snap of silk and misdirection, becoming invisible until the start of your next turn or until you make an attack roll, force a saving throw, or force an ability check, whichever comes first. As part of casting this, you may also move up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks — the last thing anyone saw of you was already the wrong direction. This is misdirection, not true invisibility, and it can be beaten by simply watching you properly: each creature that can see you at the moment you cast it makes a Wisdom (Perception) check against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. **If any one of them succeeds, the trick ends immediately for everybody** — they call out where you went, the room's eyes follow, and you are simply standing there. One person seeing through it is enough; there is never a state where you are hidden from some creatures and not others.
tricks.narration: The curtain drops for exactly one second. When it lifts you are not where anyone is looking — until somebody who was watching your feet instead of your hands points and shouts, and then the whole room is looking at you again.
tricks.sheetSummary: Invisible until the start of your next turn or until you attack or force a save or check; may move 10 ft without provoking as part of the trick. Each creature that can SEE you cast it makes a Wisdom (Perception) check vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}} — ANY success ends it for everyone. Never partial: you are hidden from all of them or none.

tricks.name: Palmed Card
tricks.flavor: There was nothing in that hand a moment ago. There is no reason for the thing in your shoulder either, and yet.
tricks.description: Your empty hand produces something with an edge and sends it on its way in the same motion. Make a {{trick attack|d20 + proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier}} against a creature you can see within range; on a hit it takes [[1d8]] psychic damage from a wound it cannot account for and will not find afterwards. Because this is an attack roll rather than a saving throw, it can be parried like any other attack — and because it is a Pledge, your Palmed feature lets you throw it inside a Turn you were casting anyway.
tricks.narration: The hand was open. You are certain the hand was open. Then there is a flick of the wrist, a sound like a card being dealt, and something is very wrong under your collarbone.
tricks.sheetSummary: Ranged trick attack ({{your trick attack|d20 + proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier}}). Hit: [[1d8]] psychic. Scales at 5/11/17. Can be parried.

tricks.name: Parting Shot
tricks.flavor: The Clone doesn't just fall. It goes out in one last burst of stagelight, and whoever struck it wishes they'd looked away.
tricks.castingTime: 1 reaction, which you take when one of your Clones is destroyed
tricks.description: When a Clone of yours is destroyed — by an attack, by Mirror Image, by Decoy Detonation, or by any other means — you can flood the space it occupied with a last flare of false light. Each creature within 5 feet of the Clone's former space must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}} or be blinded until the end of its next turn. If several of your Clones are destroyed at the same instant — a failed Mirror Image gamble takes every Clone you committed — this still triggers only once, and you choose which of their spaces flares. This trick does not create, spend, or restore any Clones on its own — it only triggers off a Clone that is already being destroyed some other way.
tricks.narration: The Clone does not just fall. It goes out in a last hard flare of stagelight, and whoever put it down is left blinking at a white afterimage where a person used to be.
tricks.sheetSummary: Reaction when a Clone is destroyed (any cause). Con save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}} or blinded until end of its next turn. Several Clones dying at once still trigger it only once — you choose whose space flares. Doesn't cost or grant Clones.

tricks.name: Peals of Laughter
tricks.flavor: You tell the joke you've been saving for exactly this moment, and it lands like a hammer.
tricks.description: You land a joke so devastatingly funny that one creature you can see within range doubles over. It must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}} or collapse in helpless laughter, resolved exactly as below. A creature immune to being charmed automatically succeeds, and a creature that cannot hear or cannot understand you is unaffected.
tricks.narration: You tell the joke you have been saving all night, and it lands like a hammer. They fold in half laughing, hating it, entirely unable to stop.
tricks.sheetSummary: One creature: Wisdom save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}} or helpless laughter. Resolution below.

options.name: Prone and helpless
options.effect: The creature falls prone and is incapacitated: it takes no actions, no bonus actions and no reactions, its speed is 0, and it cannot stand up. Being prone applies as normal on top of that — melee attacks against it have advantage, ranged attacks against it have disadvantage — and being incapacitated means it automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws.

options.name: Anyone hits it, it stops laughing
options.effect: The first time the creature takes any damage, the effect ends on it immediately — no saving throw needed. A blow snaps it out of the fit. It is still prone and must stand up as normal.

options.name: Otherwise it laughs it off in its own time
options.effect: If nobody hits it, it repeats the Wisdom saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}} at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. It also ends when the duration runs out or your concentration breaks.

tricks.name: Phantom Needle
tricks.flavor: There's no blade in your hand. That doesn't stop the audience member three rows back clutching their arm.
tricks.description: You point at a creature you can see within range, and for one vivid instant it feels exactly what a blade sliding between its ribs would feel like. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}} or take [[1d8]] psychic damage, flinching from a wound that was never there. On a success, the target takes no damage.
tricks.narration: There is no blade in your hand. You point anyway, and somewhere three rows back a body doubles over clutching a rib that has not been touched, entirely convinced.
tricks.sheetSummary: Wisdom save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. Fail: [[1d8]] psychic damage. Success: no effect.

tricks.name: Places, Everyone
tricks.flavor: The call every company knows. Wherever they were standing, they are standing somewhere better one second later.
tricks.description: You call the company to their marks. Each ally of your choice within range may immediately use its reaction to move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks. An ally with no reaction available simply does not move. Casting this costs 1 Mirth, spent as you cast; like every costed Turn it generates none back.
tricks.narration: One word, pitched to carry, in the voice that means it. Nobody argues with it and nobody is where they were.
tricks.sheetSummary: Each ally of your choice may immediately use its reaction to move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks. No reaction, no move.

tricks.name: Powder Screen
tricks.flavor: One second you're standing there. The next, there's just a lot of colored smoke and a faint, receding laugh.
tricks.description: You detonate a charge of colored smoke, filling a 15-foot cube within range with a thick, drifting haze that heavily obscures the area for the duration or until a strong wind (such as one created by a Strength check or a trick) disperses it. You can see through this smoke without penalty; every other creature treats it as any other heavily obscuring smoke.
tricks.narration: One second you are standing there. The next there is a great deal of coloured smoke and a faint, receding laugh.
tricks.sheetSummary: 15-ft cube. Heavily obscures the area for everyone except you. Dispersible by strong wind.

tricks.name: Puppet Strike
tricks.flavor: The wire goes taut, and a body that was never truly its own snaps forward or slams down like a puppet dropped mid-scene.
tricks.description: You wrench hard on a String already fixed to a creature you can see within range, forcing its own limbs to whip against itself. The target makes a Strength saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. On a failure, it takes [[2d6]] physical damage and is knocked prone. On a success, it takes half as much damage and stays standing. You must already have a String attached to the target to use this trick.
tricks.narration: The wire goes taut and a body that was never truly its own snaps forward, whipping its own limbs against itself before slamming down flat.
tricks.sheetSummary: Requires a String already on the target. Str save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. Fail: [[2d6]] physical, prone. Success: half damage only.

tricks.name: Quicksilver Guise
tricks.flavor: The face you wear is only ever a suggestion. Change the suggestion, and the room believes the new one instead.
tricks.description: You reshape your face, voice, and build into those of a specific Small or Medium humanoid you have seen before, or into a generic member of a humanoid race you have seen. Your clothing and gear don't change in appearance, but you can present them as part of the disguise. A creature that interacts with you can see through the disguise only if it succeeds on an Intelligence (Investigation) check against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. The disguise ends early if you attack, cast another trick with a visible Flourish, or dismiss it yourself (no action).
tricks.narration: Your face reorganises itself around somebody else's — the build, the voice, the way they hold their shoulders when they are tired. The clothes are still yours; the room stops noticing.
tricks.sheetSummary: Disguises you as a specific or generic humanoid seen before. Investigation check vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}} to see through. Ends on attacking or casting another visible-Flourish trick.

tricks.name: Reflected Wound
tricks.flavor: You show it a version of itself already broken, and for one sick instant its own body believes the lie.
tricks.description: You conjure a flickering reflection of a creature you can see within range, twisted into a vision of its own mortal wound. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. On a failure, it takes [[2d6]] psychic damage as its mind flinches from damage that was never real. On a success, it takes half as much damage.
tricks.narration: You show it a version of itself already broken, held up like a mirror at the wrong angle, and for one sick instant its own body believes the picture and starts hurting where the reflection is open.
tricks.sheetSummary: Wis save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. Fail: [[2d6]] psychic. Success: half damage.

tricks.name: Rigged Draw
tricks.flavor: You palm the card it needed and hand back one that guarantees it loses.
tricks.description: You gesture at a creature you can see within range, and fate quietly turns against it. Choose one creature within range; the next attack roll or ability check it makes before the start of your next turn is made with disadvantage. This has no effect on saving throws — for those, see your Gambit's Jinx.
tricks.narration: You palm the card it needed and hand back one that guarantees it loses. Nothing visible happens. It simply has a worse next few seconds than it was expecting.
tricks.sheetSummary: Target's next attack roll or ability check before the start of your next turn is made with disadvantage. Does not affect saving throws.

tricks.name: Safety Net
tricks.flavor: There's always a net under the wire. Tonight, it's you.
tricks.description: You call a quiet promise to an ally: no fall is final tonight. Choose one ally you can see within range. It gains [[1d6]] temporary hit points, and until the start of your next turn it has advantage on saving throws against being frightened or charmed. Casting this costs 1 Mirth, spent as you cast; like every costed Turn it generates none back.
tricks.narration: There is always a net under the wire. Tonight it is you — a quiet promise called across the room to someone who is about to need it.
tricks.sheetSummary: Chosen ally gains [[1d6]] temporary hit points and advantage on saves vs frightened/charmed until the start of your next turn.

tricks.name: Sleight
tricks.flavor: The first thing any performer learns: the hand is quicker than the eye, and the eye is quicker than the brain.
tricks.description: You perform a small feat of stage magic within range. You can produce a trivial effect: palm or vanish an object small enough to hide in one hand, make a coin walk across your knuckles and reappear anywhere within range, light or snuff a candle, chill or warm a mouthful of food, soil or clean an object, or create a harmless sensory flourish such as a puff of coloured smoke, a burst of confetti, or a single sour note from nowhere. The effect ends when you dismiss it, when you cast this trick again, or after 1 hour. It can never deal damage, and it can never move a creature or anything a creature is holding.
tricks.narration: Hands move, and something small stops being where everyone was looking. A coin walks your knuckles and reappears across the room, a candle gutters out, confetti happens for no reason. It is the first thing any performer learns and the last thing anyone catches you doing.
tricks.sheetSummary: Trivial stage-magic effect: vanish/palm a hand-sized object, move a coin, light or snuff a flame, clean or soil, minor sensory flourish. Up to 1 hour. No damage. Cannot affect creatures or held items.

tricks.name: Smoke and Mirrors
tricks.flavor: The stage fills with fog, mirrors unfold from nowhere, and suddenly nobody - including your enemies - can tell where anyone actually is.
tricks.description: You fill a 20-foot cube within range with a bank of illusory smoke and drifting false reflections. The area becomes heavily obscured for as long as you concentrate on this trick. The smoke has no substance - it doesn't impede movement and can't be dispersed by wind - and creatures relying on darkvision see only more illusory smoke, not through it. You may designate any number of creatures, including yourself, that see the area normally instead, letting you use the cloud as cover for yourself and your allies while it blinds everyone else.
tricks.narration: Fog rolls in and mirrors unfold out of nowhere, and suddenly nobody in the room — including the people you brought — is sure what they are looking at.
tricks.sheetSummary: Fills a 20-ft cube with illusory heavily-obscuring smoke (no wind dispersal, ignores darkvision); you may designate chosen creatures to see through it normally.

tricks.name: Something Behind You
tricks.flavor: The oldest gag in the act, and it has never once stopped working: you look past their shoulder, and their whole body believes you before their mind gets a vote.
tricks.description: You put a single vivid, wrong thing at a creature's shoulder — a shape, a breath, a hand closing — and let its own nerves do the work. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. On a failure it takes [[2d6]] psychic damage as the fright goes through it like a shock; on a success it takes half as much. This is plain, reliable damage with no rider attached — it always works the same way, which is exactly what it is for.
tricks.narration: Your eyes flick to a point just past their shoulder and your face does something honest. Whatever they turn to find is already gone, and the jolt of it hits them somewhere under the ribs.
tricks.sheetSummary: Wisdom save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. Fail: [[2d6]] psychic. Success: half damage. No rider.

tricks.name: Stage Fright
tricks.flavor: You show them, for just a heartbeat, exactly how badly this could go for them. Their body believes you completely.
tricks.description: You plant a single, perfectly convincing image of its own doom in one creature's mind within range. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. On a failure, it is frightened of you for the duration and, on each of its turns while frightened this way, must use its action to move as far away from you as it can by the safest available route, unless there is nowhere safer to move. A frightened target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. On a success, the target is unaffected.
tricks.narration: You show them, for one heartbeat, exactly how badly this could go for them. Nothing about it is real. Their body does not care.
tricks.sheetSummary: Wisdom save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. Fail: frightened, must use its action to flee each turn; repeats save at end of each turn. Success: no effect.

tricks.name: Steal Their Luck
tricks.flavor: "Watch this," you mutter, and hand your own good fortune across the ring like a stolen pocket watch.
tricks.castingTime: 1 reaction, which you take when an ally you can see within range is about to make an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw
tricks.description: You call out the number before the dice even settle. When an ally you can see within range is about to make an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can roll a d20 and have the ally use your result in place of its own (the ally still adds any modifiers it would normally apply). You must commit to using this trick before the ally's roll is revealed, and once you do, the ally must use your roll instead of its own, for better or worse.
tricks.narration: "Watch this," you mutter, and hand your own good fortune across the ring like a lifted pocket watch. It works. It always works. You just do not have it any more.
tricks.sheetSummary: Before an ally's attack roll, check, or save is revealed, roll a d20; the ally uses your d20 result (plus its own modifiers) instead of its own die.

tricks.name: Swap the Cards
tricks.flavor: The card the audience picked is never the card that comes back. Neither, tonight, is the person.
tricks.description: You and one willing creature you can see within range instantly trade places, each appearing in the space the other just left and facing however you choose. Neither of you provokes opportunity attacks from the exchange, and neither of you can be moved into a space that would not hold you. This is the Trickster's answer to a companion standing in the wrong place: pull the wounded one out of reach and put yourself, or somebody better armoured, where the trouble already is.
tricks.narration: Two quick gestures and a step that goes nowhere, and the pair of you are simply standing where the other one was. Nobody sees the move, including the person you moved.
tricks.sheetSummary: You and one willing creature you can see instantly swap places. Neither provokes opportunity attacks; neither can arrive in a space that wouldn't hold them.

tricks.name: That's the Act
tricks.duration: Until the start of your next turn
tricks.flavor: Falling over is not the failure. Falling over is the bit. The failure would be staying down.
tricks.description: You turn the whole miserable situation into the routine you have done a thousand times. Each ally of your choice within range gains [[2d6]] temporary hit points, and any of them that is prone may stand up without spending movement. Casting this costs 2 Mirth, spent as you cast; like every costed Turn it generates none back.
tricks.narration: You take the worst thing happening to your friends and play it as though it were scripted — and it works, because they would rather be in on the joke than under it.
tricks.sheetSummary: Each ally of your choice gains [[2d6]] temporary hit points, and any of them that is prone may stand without spending movement.

tricks.name: The Crowd Turns
tricks.flavor: Every performer's nightmare, handed to somebody else: the room decides it does not like you, and you can feel it happen.
tricks.description: You turn the mood of the room against creatures of your choice within a 15-foot radius of a point you can see within range. Each of them that can hear and understand you makes a Wisdom saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. On a failure it has disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of its next turn. This deals no damage. Casting this costs 2 Mirth, spent as you cast; like every costed Turn it generates none back.
tricks.narration: You do not insult them. You simply let the room know how this is going, and they feel every eye in it land on them at once.
tricks.sheetSummary: 15-ft radius. Creatures of your choice that can hear and understand you: Wisdom save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}} or disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of its next turn. No damage.

tricks.name: The Grand Illusion
tricks.flavor: Every eye in the tent turns to you at once. What they see next, they will never fully stop seeing.
components: Prop (a folding fan or opera mask)
tricks.description: You spend a surge of banked Phantasm to seize the minds of every creature you choose within a 30-foot-radius sphere centred on a point within range, showing each of them their own private, tailored nightmare all at once. Each target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. On a failure, a target takes [[5d6]] psychic damage and is frightened of you for the duration; on a success, it takes half as much damage and is not frightened. **The damage happens once, as you cast it — this trick never deals damage again on a later turn.** What lasts for the duration is the fear: a frightened target repeats the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the frightened condition on itself on a success. It requires at least 4 Phantasm banked, spent whether or not any target fails its save.
tricks.narration: Every eye in the tent turns to you at once, and what they see next they will never fully stop seeing.
tricks.sheetSummary: 30-ft-radius sphere. Wisdom save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. Fail: [[5d6]] psychic and frightened of you for the duration. Success: half damage, no fear. The damage is dealt ONCE on casting and never repeats; only the fear lasts. A frightened target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns to end it.

tricks.name: The House Wins
tricks.flavor: Everyone gets a run. Nobody gets to keep it. You are simply the one who decides when the table closes.
tricks.description: You call in everything a creature's luck has been borrowing. One creature you can see within range makes a Dexterity saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. On a failure it takes [[3d6]] physical damage and has disadvantage on the next d20 it rolls before the start of your next turn; on a success it takes half as much damage and rolls normally. Casting this costs 2 Mirth, spent as you cast; like every costed Turn it generates none back.
tricks.narration: Its run of luck does not end so much as get repossessed, all at once, with interest — and for a moment afterwards nothing it tries quite works either.
tricks.sheetSummary: Dexterity save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. Fail: [[3d6]] physical and disadvantage on its next d20 before the start of your next turn. Success: half damage only.

tricks.name: The Impossible Show
tricks.flavor: The whole tent disappears. In its place: whatever you need everyone to believe is standing here instead - a burning building, a bottomless pit, an army that was never hired.
tricks.description: A 60-foot cube within range becomes a fully realised illusory environment — sight, sound, temperature and scent — of anything you can picture. It requires no concentration and holds for the duration. It has no substance: it deals no damage, supports no weight, and does not impede anything that does not rely on sight. Any creature may spend its action to attempt an Intelligence (Investigation) check against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}} to see through it, and a creature shoving through the cube may attempt that check as part of the movement; on any success the illusion collapses immediately and entirely, for every creature at once.
tricks.narration: The tent is gone. In its place is a rockfall, or a wall of fire, or a drop into nothing — cold on your face, loud in your ears, and entirely in the way. Nobody caught inside it can think straight, because nobody fights well in the middle of a disaster they believe in. It holds until one person stops, really looks, and says so out loud — and then there was never anything there at all.
tricks.sheetSummary: 60-ft cube, no concentration. Deals no damage, supports no weight, and never blocks movement. Its effects, its one-off dramatic moment and how it can be ended early are listed below.

options.name: Blocks sight
options.effect: Line of sight cannot be traced through the cube.

options.name: Difficult terrain
options.effect: The cube's area is difficult terrain. It never blocks movement — the illusion has no substance — so any creature may enter, cross or leave it at any time, simply paying the doubled cost.

options.name: Disadvantage inside
options.effect: Every creature inside the cube, allies included, has disadvantage on every attack roll, ability check and saving throw.

options.group: Once before it ends — you choose when
options.name: The dramatic moment (bonus action)
options.effect: Each creature of your choice inside the cube or within 10 ft of it makes a Wisdom saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. On a failure it is frightened of the illusion until the end of its next turn and, if it has a reaction available, must use that reaction to move as far from the illusion as its speed allows.

options.name: Seeing through it
options.effect: A creature may spend its action to attempt an Intelligence (Investigation) check against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}, or attempt that check for free as part of moving into or through the cube. On any success the illusion collapses immediately and entirely, for every creature at once. **A failed check has no further effect:** the creature is not stuck, not stopped and not harmed — it simply still believes what it is looking at, and may move and try again as often as it likes.

tricks.name: The Prestige
tricks.flavor: Every great trick has three parts. This is the third: the part where the man who died walks back out, and the crowd never forgives you for it.
tricks.castingTime: 1 reaction, which you take when you are reduced to 0 hit points
tricks.description: The blow lands. You drop. The crowd screams — and then you walk back out from somewhere else in the room, unmarked, while the thing on the floor turns out to have been a Clone all along. You can cast this trick only if you have at least 2 Clones active when the triggering blow lands. It resolves before you are reduced to 0 hit points, so you never become incapacitated and your Clones do not drop: you fall to 1 hit point instead and spend 2 of them — the first collapses in your space wearing your wounds, and the second is the one that walks away. You teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet, and until the end of your next turn every creature that watched you fall has disadvantage on attack rolls against you — they are still looking at the body. Both Clones are spent whether or not anyone is fooled.
tricks.narration: The blow lands. You drop. The crowd screams — and then you walk back out from somewhere else in the room entirely, unmarked, while the thing crumpled on the floor turns out to have been wearing your face all along.
tricks.sheetSummary: Reaction when reduced to 0 HP. Requires and spends 2 active Clones; resolves before you drop, so your Clones never fall with you. Drop to 1 HP instead; a Clone collapses in your space wearing your wounds; teleport up to 30 ft. Creatures that saw you fall have disadvantage on attacks against you until end of your next turn.

tricks.name: The Punchline
tricks.flavor: You have been setting this up since the fight started, and they have been laughing along with everyone else. Then it lands on them.
tricks.description: You deliver the line you have been building toward at one creature that can hear and understand you within range. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. On a failure it takes [[2d6]] psychic damage; on a success it takes half as much. Casting this costs 2 Mirth, spent as you cast; like every costed Turn it generates none back. Your damage is something you build the room up to, not something you open with.
tricks.narration: The timing is everything and you have had all fight to find it. It lands somewhere behind the eyes, and the worst part is that everyone else in the room laughs.
tricks.sheetSummary: Target must hear and understand you. Wisdom save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. Fail: [[2d6]] psychic. Success: half damage.

tricks.name: The Quick Change
tricks.flavor: A different coat, a different walk, a different name if anyone asks. The performer underneath never changes.
components: Prop (a costume piece or scrap of makeup)
tricks.description: You alter your appearance - your face, your clothing, your height and build within a modest range, even your voice - for the duration. You decide the specifics, including whether you resemble a generic member of some race or a specific individual you have seen. A creature that interacts with you can determine you are disguised with a successful Intelligence (Investigation) check against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}; the disguise otherwise fools sight and casual hearing. The disguise doesn't change any of your game statistics, ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), and ends immediately if you make an attack roll or force a saving throw.
tricks.narration: A different coat, a different walk, a different name if anyone asks. The performer underneath is unchanged and would like you to keep that to yourself.
tricks.sheetSummary: Changes appearance/voice within modest limits; no stat changes. Investigation check vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}} to see through on close interaction. Ends on attack or forcing a save, or if dismissed.

tricks.name: The Suggestion
tricks.flavor: You do not tell them what to do. You tell them what they were already about to do, and they are far too polite to argue.
tricks.description: You hand one creature that can hear and understand you a course of action it believes was its own idea. Choose one option below as you cast. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}; on a failure it must obey. It is never made to harm itself or its allies, and the compulsion ends the moment it takes damage from you or your companions.

options.name: Take a walk
options.effect: On its next turn it must use its action to Dash, moving as directly away from you as its path allows. It provokes opportunity attacks as normal for leaving anyone's reach.

options.name: Put that down
options.effect: It immediately drops whatever it is holding in one hand of your choosing, and it cannot pick anything back up until the end of its next turn.

tricks.narration: You say it plainly, as though confirming something already agreed, and they nod along with a decision they never made.
tricks.sheetSummary: Target must hear and understand you. Choose an option as you cast; Wisdom save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}} or it must obey on its next turn. Never made to harm itself or its allies; ends if you or your allies damage it.

tricks.name: The Whole Audience Laughs
tricks.flavor: You deliver the biggest punchline of the show, and it lands on everyone at once. Nobody in the audience gets to not laugh.
tricks.description: You deliver the biggest punchline of the show and it lands on the whole room at once. It does two things at the same time, listed below — and the half aimed at your own company always works, whatever is standing on the other side of the room.
tricks.narration: You have been setting this up since the first round and everybody feels it arrive. Half the room goes down clutching its ribs; the other half — yours — straightens up, stops being afraid of anything, and gets back to work.
tricks.sheetSummary: Two simultaneous effects: a Wisdom save or helpless laughter on creatures of your choice, and temporary hit points plus condition removal for your allies. The ally half always works. Full resolution below.

options.name: Helpless laughter
options.effect: Each creature of your choice that you can see within range makes a Wisdom saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. On a failure it collapses in helpless laughter, as described below. A creature immune to being charmed automatically succeeds, and a creature that cannot hear or cannot understand you is unaffected.

options.name: Prone and helpless
options.effect: The creature falls prone and is incapacitated: it takes no actions, no bonus actions and no reactions, its speed is 0, and it cannot stand up. Being prone applies as normal on top of that — melee attacks against it have advantage, ranged attacks against it have disadvantage — and being incapacitated means it automatically fails Strength and Dexterity saving throws.

options.name: Anyone hits it, it stops laughing
options.effect: The first time the creature takes any damage, the effect ends on it immediately — no saving throw needed. A blow snaps it out of the fit. It is still prone and must stand up as normal.

options.name: Otherwise it laughs it off in its own time
options.effect: If nobody hits it, it repeats the Wisdom saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}} at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. It also ends when the duration runs out or your concentration breaks.

options.name: The room is on your side
options.effect: Each ally you can see within range gains [[2d6+Cha]] temporary hit points, and immediately ends any frightened or charmed condition affecting it. This half never calls for a saving throw and is never blocked by anything on the far side of the fight — constructs and undead cannot laugh, but your friends still can.

tricks.name: Vicious Jibe
tricks.flavor: You find the one thing they hate about themselves and say it louder than they can think.
tricks.description: You unleash a string of insults laced with subtle magic at a creature you can see within range that can hear you (the trick has no effect on a target that is deaf). The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}} or take [[1d6]] psychic damage and have disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the end of its next turn, too busy stewing over what you said to focus.
tricks.narration: You find the one thing they already hate about themselves and say it louder than they can think it. It lands somewhere behind the sternum, and for a moment they are not fighting you, they are arguing with you.
tricks.sheetSummary: Wis save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. Fail: [[1d6]] psychic damage, disadvantage on target's next attack roll before end of its next turn. No effect on a deaf target.

tricks.name: Waking Nightmare
tricks.flavor: You don't show them anything real. You just remind their nerves what pain used to feel like, and let the memory do the rest.
tricks.description: You reach into a creature's mind within range and make it briefly, completely certain that it is being torn apart. The target must make an Intelligence saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}, taking [[3d8]] psychic damage on a failure, or half as much damage on a success. A creature immune to being frightened has advantage on this saving throw, since the illusion has nothing to take hold of. Casting this costs 3 Phantasm — it is the payoff you bank the meter for, not something you open with, and the Phantasm is spent whether or not the target's mind gives way.
tricks.narration: You do not show them anything real. You simply remind their nerves what being torn apart used to feel like, and let the body take it from there.
tricks.sheetSummary: Intelligence save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. Fail: [[3d8]] psychic damage. Success: half. Fear-immune creatures have advantage on the save.

tricks.name: Walk It Off
tricks.flavor: You have been hit by a cannonball, a horse, and a man twice your size, and you got up every time. Mostly it is a matter of being told to.
tricks.description: You haul one ally you can see within range back into the act — a slap on the back, a hand up, a line delivered too fast to argue with. It regains [[2d6+Cha]] hit points. This is the only true healing in the circus: nobody else in the company can put hit points back, which is why a Buffoon is worth having. Casting this costs 1 Mirth, spent as you cast; like every costed Turn it generates none back.
tricks.narration: You are already talking before you reach them, and none of it is sympathetic. Somehow they are on their feet by the end of the sentence, insulted and breathing.
tricks.sheetSummary: One ally regains [[2d6+Cha]] hit points.

tricks.name: Word of Encouragement
tricks.flavor: A quick, warm aside from the wings: "You've got this, kid." Somehow, they always do.
tricks.description: You call out a quick word of encouragement to one creature you can see within range. The next time that creature makes an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw before the start of your next turn, it can add 1d4 to the roll. The creature can wait to see the roll before deciding whether to add the bonus.
tricks.narration: A quick warm aside from the wings — "you've got this, kid" — delivered like you have seen them do it a hundred times before. Somehow they always do.
tricks.sheetSummary: No save. Target may add 1d4 to its next ability check, attack roll, or save before the start of your next turn (decided after rolling).

tricks.name: Your Own Face
tricks.flavor: You do not invent anything. You simply show them the version of themselves they have been avoiding, and hold it up until they look.
tricks.description: A creature you can see within range meets its own eyes in something that should not be a mirror — older, opened up, already finished. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. On a failure it takes [[2d6]] psychic damage and is frightened of you until the end of its next turn. On a success it takes half as much damage and is not frightened.
tricks.narration: For a moment there is a second one of them standing in the room, wearing everything that is about to happen. Then there isn't, and the original will not look at you straight for the rest of the fight.
tricks.sheetSummary: Wisdom save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. Fail: [[2d6]] psychic and frightened of you until the end of its next turn. Success: half damage, no fear.

skills.name: Athletics
skills.description: Covers difficult situations while climbing, jumping, or swimming, and physical feats like grappling.
skills.narration: You get a hand on the ledge and haul, or you take a run at the gap and commit, or you get both arms around someone and refuse to let go. It is rarely graceful and it is usually loud, and it works because you were willing to put your whole body behind it.

skills.name: Acrobatics
skills.description: Staying on your feet in tricky situations, balancing, and performing acrobatic stunts.
skills.narration: The floor moves and you go with it. A rolled landing, a foot finding a beam it had no right to find, a spin out of a grab — you stay upright in places where staying upright is not really an option.

skills.name: Sleight of Hand
skills.description: Perform manual trickery like planting an item, palming an object, or picking a pocket or lock without being noticed.
skills.narration: Everything interesting happens in the half-second the other person is looking at your face. The object is gone, or arrived, or changed hands, and the only evidence is that nothing feels wrong.

skills.name: Stealth
skills.description: Conceal yourself from enemies, slip past guards, or move silently without being seen or heard.
skills.narration: You move at the speed the room can absorb. Boots off the loud board, breath held through the doorway, body in the pillar's shadow until the lamp swings past — and the guard walks by close enough to touch.

skills.name: Arcana
skills.description: Recall lore about spells, magic items, eldritch symbols, and the planes of existence.
skills.narration: You have seen this sigil before, or something close enough. The knowledge comes up the way a language does — you simply know what the shape is for, and roughly what happens to people who get it wrong.

skills.name: History
skills.description: Recall lore about historical events, legendary people, ancient kingdoms, and past disputes.
skills.narration: You know whose banner that was, which war ended it, and what everybody at the time claimed had happened instead. The name on the wall means something to you that it does not mean to anyone else in the room.

skills.name: Investigation
skills.description: Deduce clues, spot hidden details, and draw conclusions from evidence at a scene.
skills.narration: You stop looking at the scene and start reading it: the scuff going the wrong direction, the dust missing from one shelf, the drawer that was closed in a hurry. The conclusion assembles itself.

skills.name: Nature
skills.description: Recall lore about terrain, plants, animals, weather, and natural cycles.
skills.narration: You read the ground, the weather, and the treeline the way other people read a signpost. What grows here, what hunts here, what the sky is about to do.

skills.name: Religion
skills.description: Recall lore about deities, rites, prayers, religious hierarchies, and holy symbols.
skills.narration: You know the rite and you know who it is for. The hierarchy, the holy days, the symbol carved above the door and what the people who carved it wanted from it.

skills.name: Animal Handling
skills.description: Calm a domesticated animal, keep a mount from bolting, or intuit an animal's intentions.
skills.narration: You slow down, keep your hands where it can see them, and speak the way you would to someone about to bolt. It watches you, decides, and settles.

skills.name: Insight
skills.description: Determine the true intentions of a creature, such as spotting a lie or predicting its next move.
skills.narration: It is the pause before the answer, the smile that arrives a beat late, the way the story is a little too tidy. You do not catch them lying — you catch them deciding to.

skills.name: Medicine
skills.description: Stabilize a dying companion, diagnose an illness, or identify what kind of ailment afflicts someone.
skills.narration: You get to them fast, find the bleed, and put pressure where pressure has to go. Half of it is knowing what the body is doing; the other half is being the person in the room who is not panicking.

skills.name: Perception
skills.description: Spot, hear, or otherwise detect the presence of something using your senses.
skills.narration: Something registers before you have words for it — a shape in the treeline, a breath behind a door, the smell of oil where there should not be oil. You look again, properly, and there it is.

skills.name: Survival
skills.description: Follow tracks, hunt, navigate the wilderness, identify natural hazards, and predict the weather.
skills.narration: You find the track, read how old it is, and follow it. Water, shelter, weather, the difference between a safe crossing and a bad one — the wilderness stops being a hazard and becomes a set of instructions.

skills.name: Deception
skills.description: Convincingly hide the truth, either verbally or through actions, such as bluffing or disguising intent.
skills.narration: You tell it with your whole body: the easy shoulders, the unhurried eye contact, the small unimportant detail nobody would invent. The lie is not the words, it is everything around them.

skills.name: Intimidation
skills.description: Influence someone through overt threats, hostile actions, or physical violence.
skills.narration: You do not raise your voice. You close the distance, hold the look a beat past comfortable, and let them finish the sentence for themselves.

skills.name: Performance
skills.description: Delight an audience with music, dance, acting, storytelling, or other forms of entertainment.
skills.narration: You take the room. A song, a tumble, a story told with the timing you have spent years sharpening — and for as long as it lasts, everyone present is an audience and you are the reason they are quiet.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.description: Influence someone with tact, social grace, or good nature.
skills.narration: You listen first, find the thing they actually want, and hand them a version of your idea that gets it for them. By the end they are fairly sure it was their idea.

weapons.name: Aerial Ribbons
weapons.flavor: Weighted silk streamers the Acrobat conjures and whirls — equal parts spectacle, weapon, and safety line.

parryProfile.note: Flowing silk wraps and redirects an incoming blow beautifully — one of the best defensive weapons in the roster, matching the Acrobat's dodge-first identity. Its low damage (1d4, the same reach-tax the whip pays) is the deliberate tradeoff: the ribbons are a deflection and a safety line, not a killing weapon. Signature to the Acrobat.

weapons.name: Cannonball
weapons.flavor: A solid iron sphere from the human-cannonball act, hurled by hand — it lands like a falling anvil.

parryProfile.note: A cannonball is for throwing, not fending — there is nothing to parry with, and once hurled it is gone. Falls back to the brace (unarmed) case if held.

weapons.name: Conjurer's Staff
weapons.flavor: Six feet of lacquered stage prop, weighted at one end, and every illusionist in the show has cracked someone's shins with it at least once.

parryProfile.note: A long haft held in two hands is the easiest thing in the arsenal to put between yourself and a blade.

weapons.name: Control Wires
weapons.flavor: Near-invisible monofilament strung from the fingertips — it cuts, it binds, and it answers the puppeteer's will as readily as it answers his hand. In close it threatens with a duelist's reach; at distance the wires snap taut across the room to open a wound where no blade could reach. Special: you may attack with it as a melee weapon (10 ft reach) OR as a ranged weapon (range 30/60 ft), your choice each attack — a hit lets the Strings engine attach a free String at that range.

parryProfile.note: The one weapon that can parry ranged attacks as well as melee — a curtain of wire snaps up to turn aside blade or bolt alike. The Puppeteer's only real defense, though his very high Parry DC means even this rarely lands a Full Dodge. Signature to the Puppeteer.

weapons.name: Dagger
weapons.flavor: A plain, quick blade — the universal backup, easy to hide and easy to throw.

parryProfile.note: A small blade parries only passably — better than bare hands, worse than a dueling weapon. Once thrown it is gone, with nothing left in hand to parry with.

weapons.name: Harlequin's Cane
weapons.flavor: A slim jester's cane, twirled and cracked with theatrical flourish — half prop, half bludgeon, wholly unpredictable.

parryProfile.note: A twirling cane is a natural fending tool, sweeping blows aside with a showman's flourish.

weapons.name: Iron Chain
weapons.flavor: A heavy length of tent chain swung in wide arcs — it reaches, it wraps, and it hurts.

parryProfile.note: A whirling chain can catch and foul an incoming weapon at reach, so it fends a touch better than a rigid bludgeon.

weapons.name: Juggling Clubs
weapons.flavor: Weighted performance clubs spun in a blur and hurled end over end — a juggler's bread and butter, as happy to crack a skull as to catch the light.

parryProfile.note: A club still in hand parries modestly, batting a blow aside with its weighted head. Once thrown it has left your hand — nothing to guard with. How many clubs a Juggler still holds is governed by the Juggler's engine (Deflect).

weapons.name: Marotte
weapons.flavor: A fool's sceptre: your own face carved on the end of a stick, grinning, with bells. It is a joke right up until the weighted head comes round.

parryProfile.note: You catch the blow on the carved head — the little face takes it, and the bells make the whole thing sound like it was part of the act.

weapons.name: Mirror Blades
weapons.flavor: A matched pair of thin, silvered short blades — when the Doppelganger strikes, every one of its reflections seems to strike too.

parryProfile.note: Paired blades fend competently, and it's never quite clear which hand — or which of you — is holding them. Signature to the Doppelganger.

weapons.name: Phantom Blade
weapons.flavor: There is no blade. There is the certainty of a blade, held in a hand that knows exactly where a blade would be — and the wound argues for itself.

parryProfile.note: It parries because the attacker believes it will. Steel stops on nothing and the arm behind it stops with it.

weapons.name: Rapier
weapons.flavor: A duelist's blade, thin and quick — as much a defensive tool as an offensive one in the right hands.

parryProfile.note: A rapier's guard and reach make it well-suited to parrying — slightly easier than a bare-fisted defense.

weapons.name: Razor Cards
weapons.flavor: A deck of steel-edged playing cards, flicked from the fingertips faster than the eye can follow — always a winning hand.

parryProfile.note: A thrown card is gone the instant it leaves the hand — nothing to fend with. Falls back to the unarmed case if you try. Signature to the Joker.

weapons.name: Shortsword
weapons.flavor: A short, straight blade — light and quick, easy to pair and easier to hide.

parryProfile.note: A balanced short blade parries competently — neutral, neither a dedicated dueling guard like a rapier nor an improvised tool.

weapons.name: Slapstick
weapons.flavor: Two slats of wood hinged to crack like a broken bone on contact. It hurts far less than it sounds and far more than anyone expects.

parryProfile.note: You can get it in the way, but it is two bits of wood on a hinge — it slaps a blade aside rather than stopping it.

weapons.name: Strongman's Barbell
weapons.flavor: The classic loaded bar of the strongman act, swung as a two-handed bludgeon — absurd in anyone else's hands, natural in his.

parryProfile.note: A heavy bar is clumsy to fend with, but The Sandow simply braces it across an incoming blow — neutral, leaning on his class's brace rather than the weapon's finesse.

weapons.name: Throwing Knives
weapons.flavor: A matched set of balanced blades, drawn and released in the same motion — the baseline knife every circus performer learns to spin before they learn anything flashier.

parryProfile.note: A knife held in hand can parry modestly — better than bare fists, worse than a dueling blade. Once thrown it has left your hand, so you simply have nothing in that hand to parry with (the empty-hands case). How many knives a Juggler still holds is governed by the Juggler's engine.

weapons.name: Weighted Orbs
weapons.flavor: Palm-sized iron spheres kept endlessly aloft. A Firebrand sets them alight, but even cold they land like a dropped anvil.

parryProfile.note: An orb still in hand can knock a blow aside, though its round face is a clumsier guard than a club. Once thrown it is gone. How many orbs a Juggler still holds is governed by the Juggler's engine (Deflect).

weapons.name: Whip
weapons.flavor: A long braided lash that cracks like a gunshot and keeps enemies at arm's length.

parryProfile.note: At reach a whip can snap aside or tangle an incoming weapon — a neutral parry, with the added advantage of keeping the attacker a step away.

armor.name: Aerialist's Second Skin
armor.flavor: Shaved kidskin over a lattice of whalebone, fitted to one body and useless on any other. It moves before you do.

armor.name: Anvil Harness
armor.flavor: Built around a smith's anvil worn as a breastplate, counterweighted at the back so it stands you up rather than tipping you over. Absurd. Immovable.

armor.name: Beasthide Wrap
armor.flavor: Layered hides from the menagerie's beasts, roughly cured — crude, warm, and surprisingly tough.

armor.name: Boilerplate Rig
armor.flavor: Riveted iron bands over a canvas jack, built in the same shop that plates the cannon. Circus engineering: heavy, ugly, and it has never once come apart.

armor.name: Cannoneer's Plackart
armor.flavor: Off-cuts from the cannon's own barrel, curved and strapped over the gut. It has been fired at. Twice.

armor.name: Colossus Plate
armor.flavor: Full articulated plate built for the strongman act's grand finale — a walking fortress that only the mightiest can even carry.

armor.name: Conjurer's Longcoat
armor.flavor: Heavy velvet to the ankle, cut wide enough to hide a dove, a deck and both your hands. It stops nothing and conceals everything.

armor.name: Contortionist's Sheath
armor.flavor: Oiled kidskin cut on the bias so it lengthens wherever you fold. Getting into it is the hardest part of the act; getting out of anything else stops being difficult.

armor.name: Fortune-Teller's Robes
armor.flavor: Layered silks and star-charts — the working clothes of the tent mystics. No protection to speak of, but they need no training to wear, which is the whole point for someone whose defense is their mind, not their hide.

armor.name: Gladiator's Half-Plate
armor.flavor: Arena kit, polished for the crowd and shaped for the kill — breastplate, pauldrons, and nothing below the hip to slow the footwork.

armor.name: Harlequin's Brigandine
armor.flavor: Diamond-patched canvas with steel plates quilted between the colours. It reads as a costume until somebody hits it.

armor.name: Ironmonger's Chain Mail
armor.flavor: A heavy shirt of interlocking rings from the show's smith — dependable, weighty, and loud on a quiet night.

armor.name: Mentalist's Mantle
armor.flavor: Weighted at the hem and lined in something that hums faintly against the back of the neck. Whatever you are holding in your head, this keeps hold of it for you.

armor.name: Mirrorsilk Vestments
armor.flavor: Silk woven with a thread that catches light wrong, so the eye slides off the wearer and lands somewhere just behind them. Tailored, expensive, and worth it.

armor.name: Padded Motley
armor.flavor: A quilted patchwork performer's costume — soft protection under bright colors, but it rustles with every step.

armor.name: Parade Shield
armor.flavor: A round, brightly painted shield twirled in the opening march — light enough to flourish, solid enough to turn a blade.

armor.name: Pickpocket's Frock Coat
armor.flavor: Tailored by somebody who has been searched professionally and resented it. Fourteen pockets, none of them where a hand would look.

armor.name: Ringmaster's Bulwark
armor.flavor: A cage-door off the big cats' wagon, banded and re-hung on a fist grip. It has stopped a tiger. It will stop most things.

armor.name: Ropewalker's Harness
armor.flavor: Strapping across the ribs and nothing at all across the shoulders, because a rigger who cannot reach over their own head is a rigger who falls.

armor.name: Serpent-Scale Mail
armor.flavor: Overlapping enameled scales that shimmer like a snake charmer's prize — protective, but they hiss and clink when you try to move unseen. Cheaper cover than a breastplate for the same base AC, but the overlapping scales rattle — disadvantage on stealth.

armor.name: Spangled Leotard
armor.flavor: Sequins, tights, and absolutely nothing between you and the world. What it lacks in protection it returns in the freedom to bend in ways armour forbids.

armor.name: Stagelight's Raiment
armor.flavor: Layer on layer of stiffened brocade and mirrored plate-sequin — the closest thing to armour a performer can wear and still call it a costume. You are magnificent and you are audible from the back row.

armor.name: Strongman's Breastplate
armor.flavor: A fitted steel chest piece worn over the bare arms of a showman — solid protection that still lets the shoulders flex for a lift. Its edge over scale mail isn't AC — it's silence: the same 14 base, but no stealth penalty.

armor.name: Studded Showleather
armor.flavor: Polished leather set with gleaming rivets — as much showpiece as protection, and the best light armor a nimble performer can wear.

armor.name: Tamer's Bracer
armor.flavor: A forearm cage of banded steel, built for a woman who put her arm in a lion's mouth nightly and kept it. Smaller than a shield and planted twice as well.

armor.name: Trouper's Chain Shirt
armor.flavor: A light mesh worn under the costume — quiet enough to tumble in, sturdier than leather. The middle-ground medium for a performer who still wants to move.

armor.name: Tumbler's Leathers
armor.flavor: Supple, close-fitting leather that moves with the body — the acrobat's default, quiet and unrestrictive.
